The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, and ovarian cancers, as well as melanoma.
summary: Scientists discovered that activating the protein PPARD in immune cells enhances their ability to burn fat and attack tumors, slowing or stopping cancer growth in laboratory experiments. The approach showed promise against colorectal, breast, ovarian cancers, and melanoma.

title: Scientists find Nazi Germany's final reactor far from operational
content:

Analysis of surviving uranium cubes and wartime documents reveals that Germany lacked the enormous quantities of uranium and heavy water needed to make its reactor operational.  

The findings clarify that the program did not reach a functional reactor stage.
summary: Scientists investigating Nazi Germany's secret nuclear program uncovered evidence that its final experimental reactor was nowhere near as close to working as previously claimed. content:

content:

content:

The appeal specifically seeks firsthand accounts of AI’s role in crafting conversation starters and providing guidance on social interactions. It asks participants to explain the various ways AI has assisted them in the dating process, whether through generating lines or offering coaching.

The initiative aims to gather a range of experiences to better understand the effectiveness of AI in online dating scenarios.
summary: The article invites readers to share how they use AI for online dating, from chat‑up lines to social coaching. It seeks details on what worked and what didn’t.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Meta launches Muse Spark Open, claims it rivals Chinese AI models
content:
Meta launched a new open‑weight AI model, Muse Spark Open, on Thursday. The company says the model is designed to compete with, and in some cases outperform, similar products from leading Chinese developers.

Meta claims Muse excels at multi‑step reasoning and complex software engineering, positioning it as a tool that could help the firm close the gap with its Chinese rivals. The announcement comes as Meta continues to expand its AI offerings.

In a post on X, Meta’s chief of AI Alexandr Wang described Muse Spark Open as “the most capable US open‑weight model to date.”
summary: Meta launched the Muse Spark Open open-weight AI model on Thursday. The model is said to excel at multi‑step reasoning and complex software engineering, and Meta claims it rivals or outperforms similar Chinese products.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Calls Grow to Limit London Robotaxi Rollout as Drivers Protest
content:
A protest is planned at Wayve’s headquarters as Uber drivers express concern about their future and city politicians call for Transport for London to have authority over robotaxi licences. The demonstration follows the launch of the first UK robotaxi services in September, which has sparked debate over regulation and driver security.

Passengers across Britain are eager to try the new technology, with more than 100,000 people on Uber’s London waitlist. While the service has generated enthusiasm, some view it with trepidation, reflecting uncertainty about its impact on existing transport workers.

Uber driver Florentina Ghiuzan from Essex said, “I think we should all be worried. I was shocked TfL approved it so soon. I knew change would come. But I thought it would come with a solution for us.” The protest is scheduled to take place at Wayve’s headquarters.
summary: A protest is planned at Wayve HQ as Uber drivers fear for their future and city politicians demand TfL have power over licences. More than 100,000 passengers are on Uber’s London waitlist for robotaxis, which began service in September, and driver Florentina Ghiuzan from Essex says, "I think we should all be worried" about TfL's rapid approval.
author: Guardian Technology

title: England and Wales to ban porn depicting strangulation and incest from 6 November
content:
The UK government will ban pornographic content that depicts strangulation and incest in England and Wales from 6 November. The new legislation will take effect early next month, outlawing the specified material.

The ban follows recommendations from a 2025 review into pornography regulation. Campaigners welcomed the legislation, noting it was prompted by cross‑party pressure that led ministers to announce new laws earlier this year.
summary: The government announced that pornography showing strangulation and incest will be illegal in England and Wales from 6 November. The ban follows a 2025 review recommendation and was welcomed by campaigners after cross‑party pressure led ministers to act earlier this year.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Elon Musk unveils Tesla Roadster 2, billed as world’s first flying car
content:
Elon Musk unveiled what he called the “world’s first flying car” during a Tesla event, showcasing the company’s newest model, the Tesla Roadster 2. The demonstration was held at SpaceX’s rocket development and testing facility in Texas.

During the presentation, the Roadster 2 drove up a curved ramp before activating SpaceX rocket thrusters that lifted the vehicle, allowing it to fly, flip and land. Musk highlighted that the sports car is equipped with thrusters and can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in less than a second.
summary: Elon Musk demonstrated the Tesla Roadster 2 at SpaceX’s rocket development and testing facility in Texas, showing it drive up a curved ramp and use SpaceX rocket thrusters to fly, flip and land. He said the sports car can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in less than a second and called it the world’s first flying car.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Two US carriers in Arabian Sea as tanker sorties rise, Trump hints at more strikes
content:
Two United States aircraft carriers are currently operating in the Arabian Sea.  

Tanker sorties across the region are reported to be running 50 % above the level recorded in September.  

President Trump has said he has not ruled out intensified strikes after the November midterm elections.
summary: Two US aircraft carriers are in the Arabian Sea. Tanker sorties over the region are running 50% above September’s rate, and Trump has not ruled out intensified strikes after November’s midterm elections.
author: Euronews

title: Midday news bulletin covers top European and global stories on October 16, 2026
content: A midday news bulletin issued on October 16, 2026 presented a roundup of the most important stories from Europe and beyond. The bulletin highlighted the latest developments across a range of topics, including world affairs, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
summary: The bulletin provides a roundup of major stories from Europe and worldwide on October 16, 2026. It includes updates on world, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
author: Euronews

title: Putin orders seizure of five European firms operating in Russia
content:
Moscow has placed five additional European companies under state control, a move announced by President Vladimir Putin in a new decree.  

The decree targets a flooring manufacturer, a paper‑packaging firm, a hygiene‑products maker and two companies that produce metal and plastic packaging. All five firms remained in operation in Russia after the all‑out invasion of Ukraine in early 2022.  

The action continues Russia’s broader campaign of seizing foreign assets.
summary: Putin issued a decree seizing five European companies that were still operating in Russia. The firms include a flooring manufacturer, a paper packaging firm, a hygiene products maker, and two metal‑ and plastic‑packaging companies that remained active after the invasion of Ukraine in early 2022.
author: Euronews

title: Italy's nationwide ATC fault causes delays at Rome Fiumicino Airport
content:
On Friday 16 October, flight delays and cancellations disrupted operations at Rome’s Fiumicino Airport after a fault struck the data‑transmission network that supports Italy’s nationwide air traffic control system.

The network failure caused widespread interruptions to flights, prompting airlines to adjust schedules and suspend services at the capital’s main airport.
summary: Flight delays and cancellations disrupted Rome’s Fiumicino Airport on Friday 16 October. The disruption was caused by a fault in the data‑transmission network supporting Italy’s nationwide air traffic control system.
author: Euronews

title: Ukrainian drones shut all four Moscow airports overnight, cancelling dozens of flights
content:
Ukrainian drones forced the closure of all four Moscow airports overnight, prompting the cancellation of dozens of flights, officials said.

In the first 14 days of October, the airports were shut for a total of 101 hours, more than double the combined closure time recorded for the entire month of September.
summary: Ukrainian drones forced the overnight closure of all four Moscow airports, cancelling dozens of flights. In the first 14 days of October, Moscow’s airports were closed for a total of 101 hours, more than double the total for September.
author: Euronews

title: Russian missiles spark huge factory fires in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia
content:
Russian missiles struck businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia, igniting massive fires at factories in both cities. The attacks caused huge blazes that spread across the affected sites.

The incidents occurred while President Volodymyr Zelensky was meeting European leaders for talks.
summary: Russian strikes ignited massive fires at businesses in Odesa and Zaporizhzhia. President Zelensky met European leaders for talks.
author: Euronews

title: African designers spotlighted at Paris Fashion Week Spring‑Summer 2027
content:
Paris Fashion Week’s spring‑summer 2027 ready‑to‑wear collections put Africa in the spotlight. Designers highlighted the continent’s creative energy and social relevance on the global runway.

South Africa’s Laduma Ngxokolo presented his Maxhosa Africa label, emphasizing a determination to showcase African identity. In the same city, Jacques Logoh – designer and founder of Togo’s International Fashion Festival – offered African creatives a platform centered on the theme “Fashion against HIV.” Meanwhile, Mossi Traoré staged his show at Paris’s Père Lachaise Cemetery, confronting the subject of death without taboo.

Fashion can absolutely be political, when it shapes identities and questions the balance of power.
summary: Laduma Ngxokolo, through his Maxhosa Africa label, seeks to put the continent in the spotlight at Paris Fashion Week. Jacques Logoh presents a show themed "Fashion against HIV" and Mossi Traoré stages a show at Père Lachaise Cemetery to address death.
author: France 24

title: EU proposes Canada could become its first associate member
content:
The European Union is looking to strengthen ties with like‑minded allies as the international context becomes more challenging, and Canada is a key part of that effort.  

In her State of the Union speech in September, EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen announced that Canada could become an associate member of the bloc, a status that does not currently exist for any EU partner.  

If adopted, the arrangement would make Canada the EU’s first associate member.
summary: The European Union is seeking to boost ties with like‑minded allies such as Canada. In Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech in September, she announced that Canada could become an associate member, a status that does not currently exist for any EU partner.
author: France 24

title: Wyoming conservatives split as midterm elections near
content:
Wyoming, the nation’s least populated, most rural and most conservative state, is showing signs of division within the Republican Party just two weeks before the U.S. midterm elections. Reporters James André and Sylvain Rousseau traveled across the Cowboy State and observed a split among supporters of President Donald Trump.

The journalists’ on‑the‑ground reporting highlights that, despite Wyoming’s strong Republican reputation, the party aligned with Trump is not unified as the election approaches. This internal discord marks a notable development in a state traditionally viewed as a solid GOP stronghold.
summary: Wyoming is the least populated, most rural and most conservative state in the United States. With two weeks until the midterm elections, reporters James André and Sylvain Rousseau reported that the party of US President Donald Trump is deeply divided in the state.
author: France 24

title: French MEP Bernard Guetta calls Donald Trump a liar and says US not ally to Ukraine
content:
French MEP Bernard Guetta, a veteran French journalist and member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group, criticized the current U.S. president in a recent interview. Guetta called Donald Trump a liar, arguing that Trump had told the American public that Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance were responsible for the rise in diesel prices, a claim Guetta described as a pure lie.

He further accused Trump of being responsible for starting a war with Iran. Guetta also warned that without American intelligence sharing, Ukraine is becoming weaker, and he condemned the U.S. president’s perceived support for Putin against Ukraine.
summary: French journalist and commentator Bernard Guetta, a Member of the European Parliament for the centrist Renew group, called Donald Trump a liar who blamed Zelensky and the Ukrainian resistance for diesel prices and said Trump was responsible for starting a war with Iran. He said that without American intelligence sharing Ukraine is weaker and accused the U.S. president of giving a hand to Putin against Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV celebrates mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital after lung cancer surgery
content:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated a mass at Rome’s Gemelli hospital on Friday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung. Photos released by the Vatican showed the pontiff leading the service in the hospital chapel.  

Doctors reported that his recovery was progressing normally. They said further tests would determine whether the cancer had spread.
summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated mass at Rome's Gemelli hospital on Friday after surgery to remove a cancerous tumour from his right lung. Doctors said his recovery was progressing normally but further tests would show whether the cancer had spread.
author: France 24

title: Ethiopia Appoints Interim Government in Tigray Ahead of Elections
content:
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced on Friday the formation of an interim administration for the northern Tigray region. The interim government is tasked with preparing elections that the prime minister says will be held within six months.

The region had been under the control of the Tigray People’s Liberation Front, which has been in conflict with government forces since September. The renewed fighting revived a war that, between 2020 and 2022, resulted in the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people.
summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed announced the appointment of an interim administration in the northern Tigray region, which had been controlled by the Tigray People's Liberation Front and has clashed with government forces since September, and the administration will prepare for elections within six months. The recent conflict revived a war that killed hundreds of thousands between 2020 and 2022.
author: France 24

title: South African Lions player found dead in French hotel before Champions Cup match
content:
A South African rugby player for the Lions team was found dead at a hotel in France on Friday, the eve of the club’s European Champions Cup match against La Rochelle. Local media reported the fatal discovery, but the player’s identity has not yet been released.

The incident occurred just before the Lions’ debut in the Champions Cup, and no further details have been made public.
summary: A South African rugby player for the Lions was found dead at a hotel in France on Friday. The death occurred on the eve of the team's European Champions Cup game against La Rochelle, and the player's identity has not been released.
author: France 24

title: Italy cuts air traffic in half due to data transmission problems
content:
Italian authorities have halved the number of flights in the country’s airspace, citing problems with the data transmission network. The reduction follows an assessment by the ENAV authority that the issue was not caused by malicious activity.

ENAV confirmed that, despite the network trouble, flights remain safe. The authority’s statement emphasized that safety is being maintained while the data transmission problem is addressed.
summary: Italian authorities have cut air traffic in half due to problems with the data transmission network. The ENAV authority ruled out malicious activity and said flights remained safe.
author: DW World

title: Kenya reports first two confirmed Ebola cases, ministry urges calm
content:
Kenya has confirmed its first two Ebola cases, a development that has prompted urgent questions about the country’s public health preparedness and border control measures. The cases have sparked concern among health officials and the public regarding the nation's capacity to manage a potential outbreak.

In response, the health ministry has stated that there is no need for panic, indicating that authorities are monitoring the situation closely.
summary: Kenya has confirmed its first two Ebola cases, prompting urgent questions about the country's public health preparedness and border controls. The health ministry said there is no need for panic.
author: DW World

title: EU aims to boost economy with AI while safeguarding workers, safety and climate
content:
The European Union is looking to accelerate its economy through artificial intelligence, aiming to keep pace with the United States and China.  

The EU’s strategy raises questions about whether it can compete globally while also safeguarding workers, ensuring safety, and protecting the climate.
summary: The European Union is seeking to boost its economy with artificial intelligence. It aims to do so while protecting workers, safety and the climate.
author: DW World

title: Jamaican filmmakers use Sky's Possession to confront enslavement and colonial trauma
content:
Sky’s supernatural series Possession opens with a woman releasing a violent spirit from a 300‑year‑old box, a visual metaphor for colonialism and oppression returning to the surface. The scene has been highlighted by observers as emblematic of a broader shift in Jamaica’s film industry, where creators are increasingly using the island’s landscape to tell stories that confront enslavement, trauma and historical memory.

The series follows a biracial British lawyer who travels to Jamaica to investigate a multimillion‑pound inheritance dispute, only to uncover a dark, vengeful spirit linked to the plantation’s brutal colonial past. Critics describe the work as a form of “cultural reparation,” with confident Jamaican creatives reclaiming the island’s narratives on screen.
summary: Sky's supernatural series Possession shows a woman opening a 300‑year‑old box that releases a spirit symbolising colonialism and oppression. The show illustrates a shift in Jamaica’s film industry as directors employ the landscape to tell stories confronting enslavement, trauma and historical memory.
author: Guardian World

title: Pro‑Nazi chants heard before Hajduk Split vs Ajax UEFA Europa League match
content:
Croatia’s Hajduk Split hosted Ajax on Thursday in a UEFA Europa League match, but the game was preceded by chants praising a pre‑World War II regime.  

The pro‑Nazi chants were widely condemned, with observers describing the incident as unacceptable. The chants took place before the match began.
summary: Croatia's Hajduk Split hosted Ajax on Thursday in a UEFA Europa League match. Pro‑Nazi chants referencing a pre‑World War II regime were heard before the game.

title: Indian police detain Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke ahead of protest
content: Indian police detained Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, ahead of an upcoming protest. The detention was carried out by authorities in India as the demonstration approached. No further details about the reasons for the arrest or the protest were provided.
summary: Indian police detained Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party. The detention took place ahead of a protest.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN chief Antonio Guterres tests quiet diplomacy while Portugal's ex-PM seeks patient talks
content:
UN chief Antonio Guterres is testing the limits of quiet diplomacy, according to a recent analysis of his approach to international conflict resolution.

At the same time, Portugal’s ex‑PM is seeking to resolve crises through patient negotiation, emphasizing that success depends on the willingness of other leaders to act.
summary: UN chief Antonio Guterres is testing the limits of quiet diplomacy. Portugal's ex‑PM says success of his patient negotiations depends on leaders’ willingness to act.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli settlers continue pogrom amid olive harvest in occupied West Bank
content:
Israeli settlers attacked a group gathering for the olive harvest in the occupied West Bank, using clubs and guns. The assault left at least two people injured, one of whom was identified as a journalist for the Washington Post. 

The incident highlights ongoing violence by settlers during the harvest season, with weapons reported as part of the attackers’ arsenal. No further details on casualties or arrests were provided.
summary: At least two people, including Washington Post journalist, injured as settlers armed with clubs and guns attack.
author: Al Jazeera

title: India adds Bhuvneshwar Kumar for final T20 vs West Indies, Arshdeep Singh doubtful
content:
India has added fast bowler Bhuvneshwar Kumar to its squad for the fifth and final Twenty20 International against the West Indies. The selection comes as the team prepares for the series‑deciding match.

However, all-rounder Arshdeep Singh remains a doubt for the game, with his availability not confirmed.
summary: Bhuvneshwar Kumar has been added to India's squad for the fifth and final T20 of the series with West Indies. Arshdeep Singh is a doubt for the match.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli settlers attack Palestinians, beat Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine
content:
Israeli settlers carried out an attack on Palestinians harvesting olives in the West Bank, an incident described as a pogrom. The assault also targeted Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine, who was severely beaten.

Levine, a U.S. journalist, was among those injured as the settlers confronted the olive‑picking Palestinians. The episode underscores heightened violence in the area.
summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives. They severely beat Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 200 patients rescued from suspected illegal rehab centre in South Africa
content:
Patients were rescued from a suspected illegal rehabilitation centre in South Africa where they had been kept in chains.  

Authorities reported that about 200 patients were taken from the facility, which was described as overcrowded.  

Officials noted that some of the individuals had “sores all over their bodies” when they were found.
summary: Patients were rescued from a suspected illegal rehab centre in South Africa where they had been kept in chains. Some of the 200 patients were found with sores covering their bodies and housed in overcrowded rooms.
author: BBC World

title: US senators demand probe of Ukraine's Starlink speed limits
content:
U.S. senators have urged an investigation into the restrictions placed on Ukraine’s Starlink internet service.  

Ukraine reported that temporary speed limits imposed on the Starlink network disrupted its battlefield missions.  

The senators’ call for inquiry follows Kyiv’s claim that the reduced bandwidth hampered its military operations.
summary: US senators have called for an investigation into Ukraine's Starlink restrictions. Ukraine says temporary speed limits on the Starlink internet network disrupted its battlefield missions.
author: BBC World

title: Joshua Foster fined after 2‑year‑old son dies in Cyprus hotel window fall
content:
A father was fined after his two‑year‑old son died in a fall at a hotel in Cyprus.  

Joshua Foster lost control of his son while showing him the view of a water park from a window, an incident that resulted in the child’s death.  

Foster was subsequently issued a fine for the incident.
summary: Joshua Foster was fined after his 2‑year‑old son died in a fall from a hotel window in Cyprus. Foster said he lost control of his son while showing him the view of a water park from the window.
author: BBC World

title: Australia vs Samoa women's Rugby League World Cup opener in Sydney
content: Australia’s women’s Rugby League World Cup opener began today in Sydney, with the Jillaroos facing Fetu Samoa. The match kicked off with Australia already underway. During the anthem, several Samoan players were seen tearing up, a moment highlighted as special for them to represent their country on the world stage.
summary: The Jillaroos faced Fetu Samoa in the opening match of the women's Rugby League World Cup in Sydney. Several Samoan players were seen tearing up during the national anthem.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Opta analysis questions if Premier League teams must run more to win
content:
Pundits frequently criticize Premier League teams for insufficient running, prompting a question about whether distance covered correlates with match results. Following Manchester United’s loss of points against Tottenham, commentators questioned the Red Devils’ effort, citing physical statistics to support their critique.

Jamie Redknapp, speaking on Sky Sports, noted a recurring pattern where teams that run more than their opponents tend to succeed. He described running more than the opposition as a “non-negotiable” in the current Premier League, stating that teams must either cover more distance or stay close enough to make it irrelevant. Redknapp specifically highlighted that Tottenham ran five kilometers more than Manchester United in that match.
summary: Pundits often criticize teams for insufficient running, with Jamie Redknapp citing Tottenham's five-kilometer advantage over Manchester United. An Opta analyst examines whether a direct link exists between distance covered and match results.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Auctioneer David Convery Drives 332‑Lot Budds Sale, £700 Barclays Trophy Sold
content:
David Convery, an auctioneer with three decades of experience, recently led a sale of 332 lots at Budds auction house, an event he described as an “Octoberfest” of sporting memorabilia. During the auction, a Barclays Manager of the Month trophy, complete with a travel case but without an identified owner, sold for £700, exceeding its estimate. Convery is noted for having secured world-record prices in the past, including for the oldest surviving FA Cup and Pelé’s 1970 World Cup final shirt.

The article by Emma John frames this market as a marker of sport’s “rampant self-inflation,” comparable to rising transfer fees and ticket prices. The piece highlights the commercial scale of the industry, featuring items ranging from historic trophies to player memorabilia, such as the shorts associated with Eric Cantona mentioned in the title.
summary: Auctioneer David Convery led a Budds auction featuring 332 lots, including a Barclays Manager of the Month trophy that sold for £700. Convery, who has auctioned world‑record items such as the oldest FA Cup and Pelé’s 1970 World Cup shirt, has managed twice as many lots in other sales.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Martínez apologizes for outburst; Reece James undergoes surgery
content:
Gianni Infantino was informed at Thursday’s Fifa council meeting that the controversial Fifa peace prize must undergo major changes or be abolished. Several council members demanded the award be scrapped, while others called for it to be depoliticised.

Donald Trump is likely to become the only political leader to receive the prize. The Fifa football social responsibility committee will make a recommendation on the matter before the next council meeting scheduled for 16 December in Doha.
summary: Martínez apologized for his outburst. Reece James is undergoing surgery.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Carmouche shaves head to make weight for PFL flyweight world title fight
content:
Liz Carmouche shaved her head as she prepared to make weight for her upcoming PFL flyweight world title fight. The bout is scheduled to take place on Friday.

Carmouche reportedly took no chances before stepping on the scales for the event.
summary: Liz Carmouche is scheduled to fight for the PFL flyweight world title on Friday. She shaved her head to ensure she would make the required weight for the event.
author: BBC Sport

title: Kartal defeats Svitolina to reach Wuhan Open semi-finals
content: Sonay Kartal upset fifth seed Elina Svitolina in the quarter‑finals of the Wuhan Open, extending her winning streak after a long injury lay‑off and securing a spot in the tournament’s semi‑finals. The hard‑fought victory marked Kartal’s continued success following her return to competition.
summary: Sonay Kartal won a hard‑fought match against fifth seed Elina Svitolina in the quarter‑finals of the Wuhan Open. The victory continues Kartal's winning streak after a long injury lay‑off and secures her place in the semi‑finals.
author: BBC Sport

title: Former art dealer Fabian Hurzeler rises to Europe's hottest young manager
content:
Brighton’s new manager, Fabian Hurzeler, has attracted attention for his swift ascent in football management.  

Hurzeler’s career began in Germany, where he coached at the fifth‑tier level before moving to England to take charge of Brighton.  

According to reports, his progress has drawn interest from Manchester United.
summary: Brighton's Fabian Hurzeler has risen from Germany's fifth tier. He is reportedly of interest to Manchester United.
author: BBC Sport

title: Premier League 'Big Six' era may be ending
content:
The Premier League has long recognized a “Big Six” group of clubs that dominate the competition.  

The group is composed of Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur.  

Some analysts are questioning whether this era is coming to an end.
summary: The Premier League has had a defined 'Big Six' consisting of Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur. The article questions whether this era is coming to an end.
author: BBC Sport

title: Olympic sprinter Beth Dobbin now largely bedbound after ME diagnosis
content:
Beth Dobbin, who represented Great Britain as a sprinter at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, is now largely bedbound. She has been diagnosed with myalgic encephalomyelitis (ME), a debilitating illness that currently has no cure.

The condition has left Dobbin confined to bed for 22 hours a day, marking a stark contrast to her former athletic career.
summary: Beth Dobbin, who represented Great Britain in the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, is now largely bedbound. She was diagnosed with ME, a disease that has no cure.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump Claims White House Papers Belong to Him, Not Americans; Appeals Court to Weigh In
content:
An appeals court is set to decide whether Americans own the president’s papers. The question centers on the ownership of documents created in the White House.

The administration argues that these papers belong to Donald Trump, not to the American people.  

The case could ultimately be heard by the Supreme Court, which is described as conservative‑leaning.
summary: The administration says papers created in the White House belong to Donald Trump, not to the American people. The case could ultimately end up at the conservative-leaning Supreme Court.
author: NPR Politics

title: Gen Z Trump voters in focus group express regret over 2024 support
content:
Why some Gen Z voters who backed Trump now regret their decision

A focus group of eight Gen Z Trump voters reported feeling unhappy or disappointed with the state of politics. Some participants said they regret supporting him in 2024.
summary: A focus group of eight Gen Z Trump voters reported feeling unhappy or disappointed with the state of politics. Some of them said they regret supporting him in 2024.
author: NPR Politics

title: Government warns high street pedestrianisation could harm local economies
content:
Councils have been cautioned about the potential risks of high‑street pedestrianisation. The government has said that any move to ban traffic must be “well considered” before implementation.

Officials warn that removing traffic from main streets could damage local economies, highlighting the need for careful assessment before any pedestrianisation plans are adopted.
summary: The government says the process needs to be well considered. It warns that banning traffic could damage local economies.
author: BBC Politics

title: Burnham to urge Swinney to work on devolution during Scottish visit
content:
Prime Minister Burnham will use his upcoming visit to Scotland to urge First Minister Swinney to work with him on devolution.  

The trip will be Burnham’s first substantive journey to Scotland since moving into Downing Street, during which he is scheduled to speak on the issue.
summary: Burnham will urge Swinney to collaborate on devolution during his Scottish visit. The prime minister will speak on his first substantive trip to Scotland since moving into Downing Street.
author: BBC Politics

title: Early IPCC Report Completion Risks Excluding Global South Research
content:
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) is confronting an equity question about who shapes its climate science.  

Early completion of the next global climate science assessment reports could risk excluding research from the Global South.  

Such exclusion would undermine the fairness of the findings.
summary: Early completion of the next global climate science assessment reports risks excluding research from the Global South. Excluding Global South research could undermine the fairness of the findings.
author: Climate Home News

title: Antibiotic Resistance in Nairobi Gut Bacteria Displaces Healthy Microbes
content:
Good gut bacteria vs. bad: What we learned about antibiotic resistance from a community in Nairobi

Years of antibiotic use have fueled a rise in bacteria that can survive antibiotics. In a Nairobi community, these antibiotic‑resistant bacteria are competing with and displacing other bacteria that are naturally present in the human gut, where they play a critical role in maintaining good health.

The displacement of natural gut bacteria by resistant strains has led to increased illness and death from diseases that were once easily treatable with antibiotics.
summary: Years of antibiotic use in a Nairobi community have fueled a rise in bacteria that survive antibiotics. These resistant bacteria compete with and displace natural gut bacteria, leading to increased illness and death from diseases once easily treatable with antibiotics.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Depression treatment during pregnancy linked to infant brain development, study finds
content:
A new randomized trial reported in Nature Communications indicates that treating depression during pregnancy can affect infant brain development and early emotional function.  

The study found that maternal depression treatment influences the developing brain of the baby and its subsequent emotional outcomes, suggesting potential benefits of addressing depression while pregnant.
summary: Treating depression during pregnancy influences infant brain development and early emotional function. The research was published in Nature Communications.
author: Medical Xpress

title: New Perspective Explores Why Pressure Can Cause Failure or Peak Performance
content: High-stakes scenarios, such as a decisive penalty kick in a final, match point in tennis, or the last attempt in a competition, often cause well-practiced performances to break down when significant outcomes are at stake. However, pressure does not always impair performance, as some individuals achieve their best results precisely during these critical moments. Existing explanations for these varying reactions to pressure are only partial.
summary: When a lot is at stake, even a well-practiced performance can suddenly break down. Yet some people perform at their best precisely in the moments that matter most.
author: Phys.org

title: Future Arctic winter sea ice loss likely underestimated, study finds
content:
Future Arctic winter sea ice is projected to shrink by roughly 1 million square kilometers (386,000 square miles) more than earlier estimates suggested.  

The new estimate comes after researchers examined clues from a warm period that occurred about 6,000 years ago. By incorporating these ancient data into climate models, they improved the models’ reliability for predicting sea‑ice changes.  

The updated projections indicate a larger loss of winter sea ice in the Arctic than previously thought.
summary: Researchers used clues from a warm period 6,000 years ago to improve climate model reliability. The improved models indicate future Arctic winter sea ice could shrink about 1 million square kilometers more than previously thought.
author: Phys.org

title: AI’s Advances in Programming and Math Suggest Physics May Be Next Field to Be Upside-Down
content: AI has made significant advances in computer programming and mathematics, prompting speculation that physics could be the next field to experience a similar transformation. The rapid progress in these areas suggests that artificial intelligence may soon be applied to tackle complex problems in physics, potentially reshaping the discipline.
summary: AI has taken huge strides in computer programming and mathematics. Physics could be the next field to be turned upside down by AI.
author: New Scientist

title: Positive mindset may help guard against cold and flu, says columnist David Robson
content:
Can a positive mindset protect us from the sniffles?

Columnist David Robson argues that looking after your mind can help shape your immune system. He suggests that if you’re trying to avoid the worst of cold and flu season, caring for your mental well‑being may be an important factor.

title: France court blocks under‑15 social media ban as UK plans under‑16 ban
content:
Social media bans are piling up across the globe. In July, France joined Australia in restricting minors from accessing major platforms, barring children under 15 from Facebook, TikTok, and other services. The ban was later blocked by France’s top court on human‑rights grounds.  

The United Kingdom is also moving toward a similar measure, aiming to forbid children under 16 from using Facebook, TikTok, and other social‑media platforms in early 2024.
summary: In July, France joined Australia in restricting minors by barring children under 15 from major platforms, but the ban was blocked by France’s top court on human rights grounds. The United Kingdom aims to forbid kids under 16 from accessing Facebook, TikTok and other platforms in early.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: Skechers coupon codes offer 20% off sneakers, apparel and accessories
content:
Skechers coupon codes offering a 20% discount are being promoted for shoppers seeking savings on the brand’s products.  

A guide outlines steps to locate, compare and apply the best online discounts for Skechers, enabling customers to reduce the cost of comfortable sneakers, athletic apparel and accessories.  

The information focuses on maximizing savings through the use of these coupon codes.
summary: Skechers provides coupon codes that give a 20% discount. The codes can be applied to save on comfortable sneakers, athletic apparel and accessories.
author: Wired

title: Egypt's climate‑resilient “super corals” in Red Sea begin showing heat stress
content:
Egypt’s Red Sea reefs, dubbed “super corals” for their historic resistance to bleaching, are now showing signs of heat stress. Scientists note that these corals have long been immune to bleaching, a phenomenon that has puzzled researchers.

Researchers remain divided over the reasons behind this resilience, but they agree that understanding the underlying mechanisms could be crucial for protecting the corals as climate change begins to take its toll.
summary: Scientists cannot agree why Red Sea reefs have long been immune to bleaching. They hope that uncovering the reason could help protect the resilient corals as climate change takes its toll.
author: Wired

title: Benchmark says AI is weakening venture capital's rule against backing rivals
content:
Benchmark, a Silicon Valley venture‑capital firm, warned that the industry’s informal agreement not to back rival startups is weakening. The firm said the “rule against backing rivals” is becoming “harder to keep,” attributing the shift to the rise of artificial‑intelligence technologies.  

Benchmark’s observation highlights growing pressure on venture firms to invest across competing AI‑driven companies, challenging a long‑standing pact in the Valley.
summary: Benchmark says AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals. The firm notes that the Valley’s rule against backing rivals is becoming harder to keep.
author: TechCrunch

title: Snapchat and Instagram grooming becoming easier as online grooming rises
content:
Online grooming on platforms such as Snapchat and Instagram is becoming “easier,” according to recent observations. The trend coincides with a broader rise in online grooming overall.

Advocates note that children as young as five are being targeted, prompting calls for reform to address the growing threat.
summary: Online grooming is rising, with children as young as five being targeted. The increase has prompted calls for reform and highlights that grooming on Snapchat and Instagram is becoming easier.
author: BBC Technology

title: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia says China lacked ‘proper’ toilets
content:
The White House’s newly appointed press secretary, Katie Zacharia, said that China lacks “proper” toilets.  

Zacharia is already facing scrutiny over her legal credentials after providing an inconclusive answer about where she passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practicing law in the United States.
summary: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said China lacked ‘proper’ toilets. She is under scrutiny over her legal credentials after giving an inconclusive answer about where she passed the bar exam.
author: Euronews

title: Turkey's worst rainfall in 80 years causes deadly floods near Istanbul
content:
Heavy rain, described as the worst in eight decades, has caused severe flooding in areas surrounding Istanbul, Turkey. The torrential downpour turned streets into rivers, overturning vehicles and cutting off power supplies.

Emergency crews are working to clear the wreckage, but the disaster has already claimed at least three lives and left five people missing.
summary: Torrential rain turned streets into rivers near Istanbul, overturning vehicles and cutting off power. At least 3 people have died and 5 remain missing as emergency crews clear the wreckage.
author: Euronews

title: Syria arrests Ali Kayali, accused of 2013 Bayda and Baniyas civilian killings
content:
Syria announced the arrest of Ali Kayali, a 70‑year‑old militia commander known as “Mihrac Ural.” The security operation targets the individual accused of leading al‑Assad‑affiliated forces that carried out mass killings along the coast.

According to authorities, Kayali’s militia conducted summary executions of more than 450 civilians in the towns of Bayda and Baniyas during May 2013. The arrests come as part of ongoing efforts to hold those responsible for the 2013 coastal massacres accountable.
summary: Syria arrested 70‑year‑old Ali Kayali, also known as Mihrac Ural. He commanded al‑Assad‑affiliated militia forces that carried out summary executions of more than 450 civilians in Bayda and Baniyas in May 2013.
author: Euronews

title: Germany to raise tobacco tax, aiming for cigarette packs near €12 by 2030
content:
Germany plans to raise its tobacco tax, a move that could push the price of a pack of cigarettes to nearly €12 by 2030, according to the proposal outlined in the title.  

The government estimates that the tax increase will generate an additional €12 billion in revenue over the next four years.  

The projected price rise and revenue target are part of the same fiscal plan aimed at strengthening the country's tax base.
summary: Germany plans to increase its tobacco tax, which could push the price of a pack of cigarettes to close to €12 by 2030. The government expects the tax hike to raise an additional €12 billion over four years.
author: Euronews

title: Families of 34 children killed in Pakistan school roof collapse demand justice
content:
Families of 34 children killed in a school roof collapse in Pakistan are demanding justice for the tragedy.  

A senior official in Peshawar told AFP that initial reports indicated the collapse was caused by “weak infrastructure.”  

The demand for accountability follows the deaths of the 34 children in the incident.
summary: Families of 34 children killed in a school roof collapse in Pakistan are demanding justice. A senior official in Peshawar said initial reports linked the collapse to weak infrastructure.
author: Euronews

title: Ukraine's SkyFall unveils StarGate drone that transports wounded soldiers
content:
Ukraine has unveiled a flying ambulance drone that could save lives in minutes. The system was demonstrated by a Ukrainian company as a new battlefield rescue option.

Developed by SkyFall, the unmanned aircraft is called StarGate and is designed to carry a wounded soldier inside an enclosed cabin. The drone’s capacity to transport a person marks a departure from conventional medical evacuation methods.

The demonstration was filmed showing StarGate taking off, flying and landing with a person on board, illustrating its operational capabilities for rapid rescue missions.
summary: SkyFall demonstrated a battlefield rescue system featuring a drone that can carry a wounded soldier inside an enclosed cabin. The drone, named StarGate, was filmed taking off, flying and landing with a person on board.
author: Euronews

title: At least 12 killed when migrant boat sinks off Gambia
content:
At least 12 people died when a migrant boat sank off the coast of The Gambia, according to reports.

The International Organization for Migration (IOM) said that tighter controls at traditional departure points in Morocco, Mauritania and Senegal have forced some migrants seeking to reach Europe to travel farther south, including to countries such as The Gambia.
summary: At least 12 people died after a migrant boat sank off the coast of The Gambia. The IOM said tighter controls in Morocco, Mauritania and Senegal have pushed migrants toward The Gambia.
author: Euronews

title: Marseille lose 1-0 to Olympiakos for second straight Europa League defeat
content:
Marseille’s woes continued in the Europa League as the French club suffered a second straight defeat, losing 1‑0 to Olympiakos. The loss marked the side’s second loss in as many Europa League matches.

In contrast, Lyon secured a victory over Premier League side Crystal Palace, while Rennes recorded their first Europa League win of the season with a 2‑1 triumph over OFI Crete.
summary: Marseille were beaten 1-0 by Olympiakos, marking their second consecutive Europa League loss. Lyon beat Crystal Palace and Rennes secured a 2-1 victory over OFI Crete.

title: UK bookstores stock up as Sally Rooney novels pulled over Palestine Action support
content:
UK bookstores are scrambling after critically acclaimed Irish novelist Sally Rooney announced that her books could no longer be sold in the United Kingdom because of her support for the proscribed group Palestine Action.  

Rooney’s statement has prompted British booksellers to rush to stock up on her titles before distributors run out.  

The British government has banned Palestine Action, which carried out non‑violent direct action and sabotage against UK military assets believed to be working with the Israeli government; support for the group is punishable by up to 14 years in prison.
summary: Sally Rooney announced that her books could no longer be sold in the UK because of her support for the proscribed group Palestine Action. British booksellers are rushing to stock up on her works before distributors run out, and support for Palestine Action carries a penalty of up to 14 years in prison under the British government's ban.
author: France 24

title: Democrats eye Latino regret ahead of 2026 midterms after Trump’s 2024 support drops
content:
In the 2024 presidential election, 46 percent of the Latino vote helped Donald Trump win the White House. Polls taken two years later show that Latino support for Trump has fallen dramatically, with many voters citing an immigration crackdown, violent ICE raids and a spiraling cost of living as reasons for their regret.

As the 2026 midterm elections approach, Democrats are looking to recapture this segment of the electorate that once formed a core part of their base. France 24 reporters Sam Ball and Barbara Gabel interviewed Latino voters and local Democratic officials in Phoenix, Arizona, to assess whether the expressed regret among Latino voters could translate into renewed Democratic support.
summary: In 2024, a 46 percent share of the Latino vote helped propel Donald Trump to the White House. Polls two years later show Latino support for Trump has fallen sharply, with some voters expressing regret and Democrats looking to use that sentiment in the 2026 midterms.
author: France 24

title: Indian authorities close central Delhi park ahead of Cockroach Janta Party rally
content:
Indian authorities have closed a central park in the Indian capital and heightened security ahead of a rally by the youth‑led “Cockroach Janta Party.”  

The group has staged near‑daily demonstrations demanding the resignation of the national election authority chief, citing the removal of more than 130 million people from voter lists. The park closure is part of the authorities’ security measures surrounding the upcoming protest.
summary: Authorities closed a central park in the Indian capital before a protest by the youth‑led Cockroach Janta Party. The group has staged near‑daily demonstrations demanding the national election authority chief’s resignation over the removal of more than 130 million people from voter lists.
author: France 24

title: Students join Yellow Vest protest in Montbéliard, union leader questions alliance impact
content:
Students have joined the nationwide Yellow Vest demonstrations as their protests merge with broader public discontent over France’s rising cost of living.  

Genie Godula is speaking alongside Sébastien Vieille, national secretary of the SNALC teachers’ union, who says the movement faces political uncertainty, deteriorating school infrastructure and mounting fiscal constraints.  

From Montbéliard in eastern France, Vieille questioned whether aligning with larger protest movements such as the Yellow Vests will give students greater collective strength or cause their demands to become “less visible.”
summary: Student protests have merged with the broader Yellow Vest movement in France over the rising cost of living. SNALC teachers’ union national secretary Sébastien Vieille, speaking in Montbéliard, said the alliance could either strengthen students’ demands or make them less visible.
author: France 24

title: Russian tanker was carrying fertilizer, not diesel, to U.S. after Trump‑Putin diesel deal
content:
Following President Donald Trump’s October 9 announcement of an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to import Russian diesel into the United States, several pro‑Russian social‑media accounts asserted that a Russian oil tanker was already transporting thousands of barrels of diesel to the United States.

Investigations confirmed that the vessel in question was not carrying diesel but was instead loaded with fertiliser. The claim that the tanker was delivering Russian diesel to the U.S. was therefore inaccurate.
summary: After President Donald Trump's October 9 announcement of a diesel import agreement with President Vladimir Putin, pro‑Russian social media accounts claimed a Russian oil tanker was transporting diesel to the United States. The ship was actually carrying fertilizer, not diesel.
author: France 24

title: France to see mass protests on Saturday, described as a “crossroads of anger”
content:
France is poised to see a “crossroads of anger” on Saturday, as French newspapers report a call for mass protests that will unite a number of social movements. The preview appeared in a press review dated Friday, October 16.

The scheduled demonstrations are expected to bring together multiple groups, though specific organizers or turnout figures were not disclosed.
summary: French newspapers say Saturday will see mass protests that will bring together a number of social movements. The protests have been described as a “crossroads of anger.”

title: Carney says US trying to 'break' Canada as Alberta votes on independence
content: Alberta, the oil‑rich western province, is set to hold a vote that will decide whether it remains a Canadian province or begins a legal process toward separation. The referendum follows comments from Carney, who has implied that the United States is trying to “break” Canada amid the upcoming vote. The outcome of the Alberta referendum will determine the province’s future relationship with the rest of the country.
summary: Carney implied the United States is trying to “break” Canada. Alberta will vote to decide whether to remain a Canadian province or start the legal process toward separation.

title: Palestinian man wanders Gaza after Israeli strike kills his family
content:
A Palestinian man is wandering the Gaza Strip in search of a place to sleep after an Israeli strike killed his family. The loss has left him without relatives or a home.

The situation is described as “genocide” in the headline, highlighting that the man now faces life alone in Gaza with no shelter.
summary: A man is wandering Gaza searching for a place to sleep. He lost his family in an Israeli strike.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Vibe coding enables AI-built software, but free alternatives raise security concerns
content:
Vibe coding, a new AI‑driven tool that enables users to build software, is being highlighted as a potential breakthrough in development workflows.  

However, the emergence of free alternatives to established programming applications has prompted security concerns, as analysts caution that such options may lack robust safeguards.  

The debate centers on whether Vibe coding’s capabilities outweigh the risks associated with less‑secure, cost‑free software solutions.
summary: Vibe coding lets users build software with AI. Free alternatives to popular programmes raise security concerns.
author: Al Jazeera

title: World Food Day: Over a billion tonnes of food wasted while 645 million go hungry
content:
On World Food Day, officials highlighted that 645 million people are currently going hungry while more than a billion tonnes of food are wasted each year.

The stark contrast between global hunger and the scale of food loss underscores the need for actions to address waste, though specific country rankings or household‑level recommendations were not detailed in the report.
summary: On World Food Day, 645 million people are going hungry. More than a billion tonnes of food are wasted each year.

title: Netanyahu's lasting legacy seen as right‑wing opposition ahead of Israeli polls
content:
As Israel heads to the polls, analysts note that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s most enduring domestic legacy may be the right‑wing opposition he has forged.

The observation highlights the prominence of a right‑wing bloc that now stands in opposition to Netanyahu as the country prepares for its upcoming election.
summary: Israel is heading to the polls. PM Netanyahu's most enduring domestic legacy may be the right‑wing opposition he faces.

title: Israel's upcoming election to shape future of 5.5 million Palestinians
content:
Israel is holding national elections this month.  

The outcome of the vote is expected to shape the future of more than 5.5 million Palestinians, a population that does not participate in the election.  

These Palestinians have no say in the electoral process, yet the results will affect their lives.
summary: Israel is voting this month. The result will affect the future of over 5.5 million Palestinians who have no say in the election.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Zelensky seeks EU support as Trump calls him harder to deal with than Putin
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is seeking backing from European Union leaders ahead of their summit in Brussels, while U.S. President Donald Trump has launched a fresh wave of criticism against him. Trump described Zelensky as “more difficult to deal with than Putin,” intensifying the verbal dispute between the two leaders.

The president’s remarks come just before the EU leaders’ meeting in Brussels, where Zelensky is expected to rally support for Ukraine. Trump's comments add a new dimension to the diplomatic environment surrounding the summit.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is rallying EU support ahead of a meeting of EU leaders in Brussels. US President Trump launched blistering criticism, saying Zelensky is more difficult to deal with than Putin.
author: BBC World

title: Record-high ship attacks near Hormuz see 12 vessels struck in one week
content:
Ship attack reports near the Strait of Hormuz have reached a record high, coinciding with a slowdown in oil exports, according to the article’s headline.  

BBC Verify’s analysis of data from a UK maritime agency found that 12 vessels were struck in a single week, indicating a sharp increase in reported attacks in the region.
summary: Reports of ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz reached a record high, with 12 vessels reported struck in a week, according to BBC Verify analysis of UK maritime agency data. The surge in attacks coincided with a slowdown in oil exports.
author: BBC World

title: Rocket Lab Delays Neutron Launch Vehicle to 2027 Due to Carbon Fibre Issues
content:
Rocket Lab has postponed the debut of its Neutron launch vehicle to no earlier than 2027. The delay follows ongoing issues with the manufacturing of carbon fibre components used in the rocket.

The company cited persistent carbon fibre production problems as the reason for the new schedule. This marks a second postponement of the Neutron launch vehicle.

The information was reported by NASA SpaceFlight.
summary: Rocket Lab has delayed its Neutron launch vehicle again because of carbon fibre manufacturing problems. The new debut date is no earlier than 2027.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Denver Broncos defeat Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in OT, Darnold intercepted twice
content:
The Denver Broncos defeated the defending Super Bowl champions Seattle Seahawks 17‑14 in overtime on Thursday night.  Wil Lutz capped the win with a 53‑yard field goal after the game went into the extra period.

Seattle’s quarterback Darnold was intercepted twice late in the game, costing the Seahawks the victory.  The Broncos’ win improves their record to 4‑2 for the season‑opening stretch, despite an injury‑ridden roster and a struggling offense.

The Seahawks fall to 3‑3, losing for the second time in five days.  Their loss total matches the 3‑3 record they posted last season when they captured their second Super Bowl title.
summary: The Denver Broncos defeated the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime, with Wil Lutz kicking a 53‑yard field goal. Quarterback Darnold was intercepted twice late in the game, and the Broncos improved to a 4‑2 record while the Seahawks fell to 3‑3.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Martin O'Neill defiant after Celtic lose twice in Europa League
content:
Celtic have now lost two Europa League group games and two derbies, leaving the club on a difficult run of results.  

Despite the defeats, manager Martin O’Neill remains defiant, insisting he can see positive signs in the team’s performance.  

The club’s nickname, “flat‑track bullies,” has once again failed a big test, according to the club’s own assessment.
summary: Celtic have lost two Europa League group games and two derbies. Martin O'Neill says he can see positive signs.
author: BBC Sport

title: FDA submits peptide interim access policy to White House
content:
The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has submitted a peptide “interim access policy” to the White House for review, according to a government filing. The policy would allow compounding pharmacies to temporarily produce and sell peptides that have previously been restricted.

The filing was presented by the Coalition to Strengthen America’s Healthcare. The policy is part of a broader effort to expand access to peptide therapies, with the FDA seeking executive review before any changes are implemented.

The White House has not yet issued a response to the FDA’s proposal.
summary: The Food and Drug Administration this week submitted a peptide “interim access policy” to the White House for review, according to a government filing. The policy would reportedly allow compounding pharmacies to temporarily produce and sell previously restricted peptides.
author: The Hill

title: Noem no longer serves as special envoy to Shield of the Americas
content:
Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the Trump administration’s special envoy to the “Shield of the Americas” coalition, the State Department confirmed.

State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott told NewsNation, The Hill’s broadcasting partner, that Noem’s time had come to… in an interview with NewsNation’s Kellie Meyer on Thursday evening.

The confirmation was issued by the State Department spokesperson.
summary: State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott confirmed that Kristi Noem is no longer serving as the special envoy to the Shield of the Americas coalition. Pigott made this statement in an interview with NewsNation on Thursday evening.
author: The Hill

title: Collins and Jackson trade jabs in final Maine Senate debate
content:
Sen. Susan Collins (R‑Maine) faced off against Democratic candidate Troy Jackson on Thursday in the final Senate debate before Maine voters head to the polls. The two candidates traded jabs over President Trump, campaign financing, immigration reform and their voting record as the Senate race enters its final stretch.

Collins highlighted her bipartisan approach to voting during the exchange, while Jackson countered on the same issues. The debate marked the last opportunity for voters to hear directly from the candidates before casting their ballots.
summary: Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic candidate Troy Jackson held their final Senate debate before Maine voters head to the polls. The candidates exchanged criticism regarding President Trump, campaign financing, immigration reform, and their voting records.
author: The Hill

title: Massie urges Trump to fire Hegseth before impeachment vote
content: Rep. Thomas Massie (R‑Ky.) urged President Trump to remove Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth before the House moves to vote on impeachment. The Kentucky Republican, who often finds himself in the crosshairs of Trump for frequently breaking with the party, made the comment in response to a report claiming the president was considering firing the defense secretary.
summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) said President Trump should remove Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth before the House votes to impeach him. He responded to a report claiming Trump was considering firing Hegseth.
author: The Hill

title: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia Confirms She Did Not Pass Bar Exam
content:
Katie Zacharia, the White House press secretary, confirmed late Thursday that she had not passed the bar exam. The statement came after questions arose about her legal background before she joined the Trump administration.

Zacharia had previously claimed to be a lawyer and President Trump had referred to her as an “attorney.” Her qualifications were scrutinized during her first week in the role.
summary: White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said she did not pass the bar exam. Her legal background was questioned after she joined the Trump administration.
author: The Hill

title: Longer Sleep Duration Linked to Higher Risk of Diabetic Nephropathy in Adults with Type 2 Diabetes
content: A recent study published online on Oct. 8 in the Journal of the Endocrine Society found that adults with type 2 diabetes who sleep longer have a higher risk of developing diabetic nephropathy and of experiencing its progression. The research links extended sleep duration with increased incidence and worsening of kidney disease in this population.
summary: A study published online Oct. 8 in the Journal of the Endocrine Society found that adults with type 2 diabetes who sleep longer have an increased risk for incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy. The study links longer sleep duration with a higher risk of both developing and worsening diabetic nephropathy among adults with type 2 diabetes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study finds undeclared active ingredients in one-third of online OTC skin products
content:
A recent study published online on Oct. 8 in JAMA Network Open reports that undeclared pharmacologically active ingredients (UPAIs) were detected in one‑third of over‑the‑counter (OTC) skin products sold online.

The research highlights a significant presence of unlisted active compounds in a substantial portion of OTC skin products available through online marketplaces.
summary: Undeclared pharmacologically active ingredients (UPAIs) are detected in one-third of over-the-counter skin products marketed online. The finding was reported in a study published online Oct. 8 in JAMA Network Open.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Online sports betting linked to increased depression and anxiety treatment
content:
Online sports betting linked to rise in depression and anxiety treatment

More people are receiving treatment for depression and anxiety in states that legalized online sports betting.

The increase in mental‑health care usage is reported specifically in states where online sports betting has been legalized.
summary: States that legalized online sports betting see more people receiving treatment for depression and anxiety. The increase in treatment correlates with the legalization of online sports betting.
author: Medical Xpress

title: American Journal of Gastroenterology Publishes Cirrhosis Preventive Care Guidelines
content:
Recommendations developed for preventive care in cirrhosis

Clinical guidelines detailing preventive care for patients with cirrhosis were published online on Oct. 5 in the American Journal of Gastroenterology. The guidelines outline new recommendations for managing and preventing complications in this patient population.
summary: Recommendations have been developed for preventive care of patients with cirrhosis, according to clinical guidelines published online Oct. 5 in the American Journal of Gastroenterology.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Same-day Metagenomics Test Detects Hidden Infections in Critically Ill Children
content:
Same‑day testing is now helping doctors identify hidden infections in critically ill children. The new approach allows clinicians to quickly detect pathogens that may otherwise go unnoticed in intensive care settings.

Metagenomics offers a new way of detecting infections in intensive care patients.
summary: A same-day test helps doctors detect hidden infections in critically ill children. Metagenomics offers a new way of detecting infections in intensive care patients.
author: BBC Health

title: Animated films still feature overwhelmingly male nonhuman characters
content:
Female protagonists in animated films have evolved significantly over the past several decades. The 1959 Disney classic Sleeping Beauty illustrates early portrayals of women in animation.

In Sleeping Beauty, Princess Aurora is depicted as soft‑spoken and vulnerable. She is cursed as an infant by the evil fairy Maleficent and ultimately rescued not by her own wits but by a prince's kiss.
summary: Female protagonists in animated films have progressed over decades. In the 1959 film Sleeping Beauty, Princess Aurora is cursed by Maleficent and ultimately saved by a prince's kiss.
author: Phys.org

title: OSU Student Finds Extra Weight May Impact Dogs' Brain Health
content:
Scientists are expanding their understanding of aging beyond humans, focusing now on dogs. Research suggests that carrying extra weight may impact a dog's cognitive health, highlighting the need for further study.

Alexandra Genualdi, a student at Oklahoma State University, presented her findings at the American Physiological Society’s 2026 Comparative Physiology conference in Orlando in September. Genualdi discussed her efforts to investigate how obesity affects canine brain function.

The study underscores that while human aging has been extensively studied, the effects of weight on dogs’ cognitive health remain an emerging area of research.
summary: Scientists have learned a lot about human aging, but still need to learn more about how other species age, including dogs. Alexandra Genualdi, an Oklahoma State University student, presented research in September at the American Physiological Society's 2026 Comparative Physiology conference in Orlando, showing that carrying extra weight could affect a dog's cognitive health.
author: Phys.org

title: Barn owl family nests in Upper West Side water tower near Central Park
content:
A rare family of barn owls has moved into Manhattan’s Upper West Side, nesting in a water tower atop a building near Central Park. The owls have taken residence in the high‑rise structure, creating a new point of interest for residents and visitors.

New Yorkers are captivated by the unexpected visitors, watching the owls from balconies and street corners as they settle into their new urban habitat.
summary: A family of barn owls has nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park on Manhattan's Upper West Side. Residents of the Upper West Side have been reveling in the birds' presence.
author: Phys.org

title: Canada’s endangered species face extensive delays in protection under SARA
content:
Endangered species in Canada are encountering extensive delays in receiving protection, according to recent reporting.  

For more than 20 years, Canada’s Species at Risk Act (SARA) has served as the legal framework for safeguarding wildlife at risk of loss from Canadian lands and waters. Under the act, once a species is classified as extirpated, endangered or threatened, it becomes illegal to kill, harm or capture the animal, to damage its residences, and its critical habitat must be protected, at least on federal land.  

The ongoing delays in listing and protecting species highlight challenges in the implementation of SARA’s protections.
summary: Endangered species in Canada face extensive delays in receiving protection. Under the Species at Risk Act, listed species become illegal to kill, harm or capture, and their critical habitat must be protected on federal land.
author: Phys.org

title: Professor Damian Helbling creates first detailed map of PFAS in Finger Lakes
content:
A first in‑depth map of per‑ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the Finger Lakes region has been produced, highlighting the presence of the so‑called “forever chemicals” in local water bodies. The effort was led by professor Damian Helbling, who in 2023 began receiving a surge of calls and emails from Ithacan residents and others after the Environmental Protection Agency announced new regulations to limit PFAS in drinking water.

Residents asked about PFAS levels in the ponds, lakes, streams and creeks near their homes, prompting Helbling’s team to compile detailed measurements across the watershed. The resulting map provides the most comprehensive view to date of PFAS contamination in the Finger Lakes area.
summary: In 2023, professor Damian Helbling began receiving calls after the EPA announced new limits on PFAS in drinking water. He produced the first in‑depth map of PFAS contamination in the Finger Lakes region’s ponds, lakes, streams and creeks.
author: Phys.org

title: BeBox is a Haiku app that emulates Be Inc.'s BeBox
content:
BeBox, a Haiku operating system application, replicates the functionality of the original Be Inc. BeBox computer. The project is hosted on GitHub at https://github.com/johnrash/bebox.

The application has drawn attention on Hacker News, receiving 35 points and generating nine comments on the discussion thread (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50111742).
summary: BeBox is a Haiku application that emulates Be Inc.'s BeBox. The project is hosted on GitHub and has received 35 points and 9 comments on Hacker News.

title: Meta to scrape business accounts' websites with consent starting Oct 30
content:
Meta announced that, beginning October 30, business accounts will be required to consent to the company’s scraping of their websites. The change applies to all business‑type accounts that use Meta’s platforms.

The new terms will allow Meta to collect data from the sites of consenting business accounts, according to the announcement. No further details about the scope or implementation were provided in the source.
summary: Business accounts will consent to Meta scraping their websites. The consent takes effect on Oct. 30.
author: Hacker News

title: Tool lets Mac windows appear on iPhone and iPad
content:
A GitHub repository titled “Any window from your Mac, on your iPhone and iPad” has been posted by the user Saffsanity. The project, named sill, is hosted at https://github.com/Saffsanity/sill.

The repository has attracted attention on Hacker News, earning 55 points and generating eight comments. The discussion thread is available at https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50112739.
summary: An article on GitHub describes a way to view any Mac window on an iPhone and iPad. The post earned 55 points and eight comments on Hacker News.
