title: PSG outclass Manchester City in Champions League as Aston Villa thrashes Fenerbahce
content:
Paris Saint-Germain asserted their status as the benchmark in European club football by defeating Manchester City during the Champions League’s return from the international break. The match marked a homecoming for Pep Guardiola’s team, but their performance was overshadowed by PSG’s display.

In other action, Prince William attended the match between his favorite team, Aston Villa, and Fenerbahce. The English club secured a decisive 6-0 victory in the contest.

The competition’s latest round also highlighted Italy’s search for a new saviour, while an Italian-German dilemma emerged as part of the broader narrative of the tournament.
summary: Paris Saint-Germain defeated Manchester City to demonstrate their status as the benchmark in European club football. Aston Villa secured a 6-0 victory over Fenerbahce in a match attended by Prince William.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia edges New Zealand in Rugby League World Cup opener
content:
Kalyn Ponga starred for New Zealand in the Rugby League World Cup opener at Sydney’s Allianz Stadium, although Australia ultimately edged the match. The game served as a fiery demonstration that the tournament is up for grabs, highlighting the impact of new rules that encourage players to swap nations. This cultural shift has generated mixed reactions, delighting some while offending others, but the intense atmosphere on the pitch has been a win for both players and fans.

The opening ceremony featured an elaborate production with fireworks, lasers, and shimmering projections, transforming the stadium into a spectacle reminiscent of a Las Vegas casino. This event marked the beginning of a bold new era for the sport, which has significantly rejigged its tournament format. The number of competing nations was reduced from 16 to 10, and the total number of matches was boiled down from 31 to 18 to distill the talent pool.
summary: Australia defeated New Zealand in the Rugby League World Cup opener at Allianz Stadium, where Kalyn Ponga starred for the Kiwis. The match marked the start of a reformed tournament that reduced competing nations from 16 to 10 and total matches from 31 to 18.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Alex Scott quits Disney+ role as Women’s Champions League presenter
content:
Former Football Focus host Alex Scott has departed from her position as a presenter for the Women’s Champions League coverage on Disney+. The departure was Scott’s decision, as she chooses to focus on other professional projects.

Among her new endeavors is the show One More Word WSL, which she will host alongside fellow former England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams. This move comes after Disney+ faced criticism following the opening round of the current season.
summary: Scott walking away to focus on other projectsDisney+ was criticised after opening round this seasonAlex Scott, the former Football Focus host, has left her role as a presenter of the Women’s Champions League coverage on Disney+. It is understood it was Scott’s decision to walk away and focus on other projects, including her new show, One More Word WSL, with her fellow former England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams.

title: Tom Willis to face Gloucester as England No 8 depth debate intensifies
content:
Bordeaux No 8 Tom Willis will face Gloucester in the Champions Cup on Friday, a match that highlights the significant gap he leaves in England’s squad depth. Although England head coach Steve Borthwick has the option to select one player based outside England for the World Cup, the consensus suggests Jack Willis, the Toulouse captain, as the likely choice. However, the article notes that Borthwick would strongly prefer to select Tom Willis, whose departure for France following an enhanced contract was described as unprecedented.

Willis is currently performing at a high level for Bordeaux, with the source describing his impact as "pulling up trees, forests and anything else in his way." The piece emphasizes that England’s No 8 position lacks depth, making Willis a player Borthwick would value highly. The upcoming Champions Cup match serves to underscore the quality of rugby England is missing due to his absence from the domestic league.
summary: Tom Willis is set to play for Bordeaux against Gloucester in the Champions Cup, highlighting a significant gap in England's No 8 options. Steve Borthwick is reportedly considering selecting the Toulouse-based player for the World Cup despite his move to France.

title: Trump hosts Rose Garden lunch to honor first responders
content:
President Trump hosted a lunch in the White House Rose Garden on Thursday to honor first responders, including law enforcement officers and firefighters. The event was designed to recognize the contributions of these public safety professionals.

Representatives from several national organizations attended the gathering, including the Fraternal Order of Police, the International Association of Fire Fighters, and the National Sheriffs’ Association. A White House official confirmed the participation of these groups in the event.
summary: President Trump is hosting a lunch in the Rose Garden on Thursday to honor first responders, including law enforcement officers and firefighters. The event brings together representatives from the Fraternal Order of Police, International Association of Fire Fighters, and National Sheriffs’ Association.

title: Fox News poll finds government corruption top voter concern, beating inflation
content:
A recent Fox News poll found that government corruption is the top concern for voters, surpassing inflation and healthcare. Six in 10 respondents stated they were extremely concerned about the issue, while nearly 90 percent of the 1,202 participants indicated they were either extremely or very concerned about government corruption.

The survey results place corruption just ahead of inflation as the primary worry for respondents, highlighting its prominence over other major issues such as healthcare.
summary: Six in 10 respondents to a Fox News poll said they were extremely concerned about government corruption, placing it ahead of inflation and healthcare. Nearly 90 percent of the 1,202 respondents reported being either extremely or very concerned about the issue.
author: The Hill

title: Lawmakers urge GAO review of wild horse sales to close slaughter loophole
content: A bipartisan group of lawmakers has requested a Government Accountability Office review of the Bureau of Land Management’s Wild Horse and Burro Sale Program. The officials aim to address significant gaps in post-sale oversight and prevent animals from entering the slaughter pipeline.
summary: A bipartisan group of lawmakers requested a Government Accountability Office review of the Bureau of Land Management's Wild Horse and Burro Sale Program. They aim to address gaps in post-sale oversight and prevent animals from entering the slaughter pipeline.
author: The Hill

title: Live WWII grenades found at Texas estate sale
content: The Austin Police Department reported that live World War II grenades were discovered at an estate sale in Texas. Authorities confirmed that no crime was involved in the incident. The discovery serves as a reminder to the public to avoid handling old military weapons.
summary: Austin Police Department confirmed that live World War II grenades were discovered at a Texas estate sale. Authorities stated that no crime occurred but warned the public not to touch old military weapons.
author: The Hill

title: India's US ambassador condemns Jayapal's criticism of voter roll revisions
content:
Vinay Mohan Kwatra, India’s ambassador to the U.S., condemned remarks made by Rep. Pramila Jayapal (D-Wash.) regarding recent protests in India. Kwatra described Jayapal’s comments on the nationwide revision of voter lists as an “unacceptable interference in India’s internal affairs.”

In his response, Kwatra asserted that India is a vibrant democracy characterized by robust, independent constitutional institutions and a longstanding record of free and fair elections.
summary: India's ambassador to the U.S., Vinay Mohan Kwatra, described Rep. Pramila Jayapal's remarks on voter list protests as unacceptable interference in internal affairs. Kwatra defended India as a vibrant democracy with independent constitutional institutions and a record of free and fair elections.
author: The Hill

title: Poll: Democrats favorable to socialism, have no idea how to pay for it
content:
A recent poll indicates that Democrats generally hold a favorable view of socialism, despite lacking a clear understanding of how to fund such policies. The data highlights a disconnect between ideological support and practical financial planning within the party.

Critics argue that individuals who support socialism while opposing tax increases should anticipate significant legislative action from newly elected Democratic lawmakers. The commentary suggests that this new cohort of legislators is likely to implement measures that may conflict with the tax aversion expressed by some supporters.
summary: A poll indicates that Democrats hold a favorable view of socialism. However, the data shows they do not know how to pay for it.
author: The Hill

title: Trump to campaign in Iowa on Oct. 22 and Nov. 1
content:
Iowa Republican Party Chairman Jeff Kaufmann announced on Thursday that President Trump plans to campaign in Iowa twice before Election Day. Kaufmann stated that he recently spoke with the President, who confirmed his intent to visit the Hawkeye State on October 22 and November 1.

According to Kaufmann, President Trump is eager for Iowans to hear his message during these upcoming visits.
summary: Iowa Republican Party Chairman Jeff Kaufmann stated that President Trump will visit the state twice before Election Day. Trump is scheduled to be in Iowa on October 22 and November 1 to share his message with Iowans.
author: The Hill

title: Trump cancels Hegseth's plan to livestream execution of Nidal Malik Hasan
content:
President Trump announced on Thursday that the planned livestreamed execution of Nidal Malik Hasan would not proceed. Hasan, a former U.S. Army major, was convicted of killing 13 people during the 2009 attack on Fort Hood.

The decision came in response to significant criticism surrounding Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s original proposal. Trump stated that while Hasan deserved to be executed, the specific method of broadcasting the event would be abandoned.
summary: President Trump stated that the livestreamed execution of former U.S. Army major Nidal Malik Hasan would not proceed. This decision followed substantial criticism of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's original plan.
author: The Hill

title: Musk and Bezos race to colonize moon and launch satellites
content: Atlantic writer Josh Tyrangiel identifies Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos as the primary rivals in the race for control of outer space. According to Tyrangiel, both entrepreneurs share the objective of colonizing the moon, mining its resources, and launching thousands of additional satellites. Tyrangiel argues that the only genuine competition for these goals is between Musk and Bezos themselves.
summary: Josh Tyrangiel states that Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos both aim to colonize the moon and mine its resources. He adds that their plans include launching thousands more satellites, with each man being the other's only real competition.

title: Burnham seeks records review of former Man City links
content: Prime Minister Keir Starmer, referred to as the PM in the report, has requested a "manual trawl" of records concerning his former links with Manchester City. This action follows fresh questions raised about hospitality dinners the Prime Minister attended while the club was found guilty of Premier League rule breaches.
summary: The PM has requested a manual review of records regarding his former links to Manchester City. This request follows the club's conviction for Premier League rule breaches.

title: Former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson sentenced to 15 years for child sex abuse
content:
Jeffrey Donaldson, a former leader of the Democratic Unionist Party, has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sex abuse. The sentence follows his conviction on 18 counts of sex abuse, which included one count of rape.

The offenses were committed against two women when they were children.
summary: Jeffrey Donaldson was sentenced to 15 years in prison for child sex abuse. He was convicted of 18 counts, including one of rape, committed against two women when they were children.

title: Farage defends Reform vetting after councillors filmed making racist comments
content: Reform leader Nigel Farage has defended his party's vetting process following the release of undercover footage showing party activists making racist comments. Farage stated that it is impossible to vet individuals for comments they may make in the future, responding to the revelations about the conduct of the party's local members.
summary: Farage defended Reform's vetting policy after councillors were filmed making racist comments. He said that you can't vet for future comments.

title: Equality watchdog writes to Greens after MPs report party over Zionism is racism motion
content: Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) officials wrote to the Green Party regarding its motion that “Zionism is racism.” The motion was reported to the EHRC by Members of Parliament and antisemitism campaigners. The letter from the watchdog addresses the concerns raised by these parties over the motion’s content.
summary: The Equality and Human Rights Commission was reported to about the Greens by MPs and antisemitism campaigners. The commission wrote to the Greens about their motion that labels Zionism as racism.
author: BBC Politics

title: Aortic root enlargement technique lets surgeons implant valves at least two sizes larger
content: A small aortic root can restrict the size of the prosthetic valve implanted during aortic valve replacement. This limitation can result in a patient-prosthesis mismatch, where the new valve is too small for the patient’s body. Such a mismatch forces the heart to work against increased resistance, a condition associated with poorer clinical outcomes.
summary: A new aortic root enlargement technique enables surgeons to place prosthetic heart valves that are at least two sizes larger than previously possible. Using a larger valve helps avoid patient‑prosthesis mismatch, which is linked to poorer clinical outcomes when the valve is too small for the patient’s body.
author: Medical Xpress

title: GLP-1s Linked to Lower Psychiatric Risk in Schizophrenia and Type 2 Diabetes
content:
New research published in The Lancet Psychiatry indicates that treatment with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1s) is associated with reduced risks of psychiatric hospitalization and emergency department visits among individuals diagnosed with both schizophrenia and type 2 diabetes.

The study found that these benefits were observed when comparing GLP-1 treatment to no GLP-1 treatment or the use of newer diabetes medications, suggesting a potential link between the conditions and a therapeutic avenue for managing associated risks.
summary: New research published in The Lancet Psychiatry found that GLP-1 treatment is associated with lower risks of psychiatric hospitalization and emergency visits in people with both schizophrenia and type 2 diabetes. This benefit was observed compared with no GLP-1 treatment or treatment with newer diabetes medications.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study links children's caffeine intake to shorter sleep and brain development changes
content: A study led by researchers at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology & Neuroscience (IoPPN) at King's College London has found that young people who consume more caffeine sleep less and exhibit minor differences in brain development. The research, published in Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging, indicates that the majority of caffeine intake among these young participants came from soft drinks.
summary: A study led by King's College London researchers found that young people consuming more caffeine sleep less. The research also identified small differences in how their brains are developing.
author: Medical Xpress

title: California Health Survey Links 2025 Wildfires to Health Issues
content:
New annual data from the California Health Interview Survey (CHIS) released today offers a detailed examination of the health impacts of the 2025 wildfires on Californians. The survey also highlights concerning health trends affecting immigrants, low-income individuals, and transgender and gender-expansive communities.

The report identifies wildfires, heat waves, and barriers to accessing medical care as significant health-related challenges facing the state’s population. These findings provide a more precise understanding of how recent environmental events have influenced overall well-being in California.
summary: New annual California Health Interview Survey data released today examines the health impacts of the 2025 wildfires on Californians. The report also identifies troubling health trends among immigrants, low-income individuals, and transgender and gender-expansive communities.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study Finds 1 in 4 Active-Duty US Army Men May Have Low Testosterone
content:
New research from the Pennington Biomedical Research Center, published this week in JAMA, indicates that approximately one in four active-duty male U.S. Army personnel may have a morning testosterone measurement below a commonly used clinical threshold. The study provides estimates of low testosterone screening results across the active-duty Army population.

These findings offer insight into the potential implications of implementing routine testosterone screening for military personnel.
summary: New research from Pennington Biomedical Research Center indicates that approximately one in four active-duty male U.S. Army personnel may have a morning testosterone measurement below a commonly used clinical threshold. The study, published in JAMA, provides estimates of low testosterone screening results to offer insight into the implications of routine screening for military personnel.

title: Intensive blood pressure control protects heart without added kidney failure risk
content: High blood pressure forces the heart to work harder to pump blood, a strain that can thicken the heart muscle and narrow arteries over time. This condition complicates cardiovascular health, and even in individuals with no other health conditions, a 20 mmHg rise in blood pressure doubles the risk of dying from heart disease.
summary: High blood pressure forces the heart to work harder, which can thicken the heart muscle and narrow arteries. A 20 mmHg rise in blood pressure doubles the risk of dying from heart disease even in people with no other health conditions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Experts propose reframing traumatic brain and spinal cord injuries as chronic disorders
content:
A new paper published in The Lancet Neurology proposes a fundamental shift in the understanding and management of traumatic brain and spinal cord injuries in adults. Titled "Reframing traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury as chronic multisystem disorders: toward integrated, long-term care," the article advocates for viewing these conditions as chronic multisystem disorders rather than acute events.

The proposal is authored by international experts from various institutions and disciplines. The paper aims to establish a framework for integrated, long-term care that aligns with the chronic nature of these injuries.
summary: A new paper in The Lancet Neurology proposes a fundamental shift in how traumatic brain and spinal cord injuries in adults are understood and managed. International experts suggest reframing these conditions as chronic multisystem disorders to enable integrated, long-term care.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Antonia Okonma Shittu's chemo-inspired wig business now worn by A-list stars
content:
Antonia Okonma Shittu launched her wig business following a shock diagnosis that resulted in her losing her hair to chemotherapy. Her enterprise has since grown to the point where her wigs are now worn by A-list stars.

Shittu stated that her motivation for the business is to help other women feel their best.
summary: Antonia Okonma Shittu launched her wig business after receiving a shock diagnosis. Her wigs are now worn by A-list stars, and she aims to help other women feel their best.
author: BBC Health

title: NHS England guidance directs trans patients to wards matching biological sex
content: NHS England has issued new guidance stating that trans patients should receive care on single-sex hospital wards or bays that correspond to their biological sex. The directive specifies that hospital spaces should be allocated based on biological sex rather than gender identity.
summary: New NHS England guidance states that trans patients should be cared for on single-sex hospital wards or bays. The spaces must align with the patient's biological sex.
author: BBC Health
